Cleaning FAQ

Q: How much does a house cleaner cost in London?

Regular weekly or fortnightly cleans start at £27 per hour with Hausio, with a 5-hour minimum. One-off cleans are £30/hr, deep cleans £45/hr, end-of-tenancy £32/hr. Cleaning products can be added for £15 per visit; you can also supply your own. Bookings inside the Central London Congestion Zone (EC, WC, W1, SW1, SE1) carry a flat £18 access charge.

Q: How long should a deep clean take in a London flat?

A 1-bed flat usually needs 5 hours or more, a 2-bed 5–7 hours, and a 3-bed house 7–9 hours. End-of-tenancy cleans add 1–2 hours for oven, fridge and limescale work that letting agents expect for the deposit return.

Q: Do you offer end-of-tenancy cleans with deposit-back guarantee?

Yes. Our end-of-tenancy clean follows the checklist used by most major London letting agents. If your landlord or agent flags a cleaning issue within 72 hours of completion, we return free of charge to fix it.

Man and Van · London

# London man and van — fully insured, fairly priced.

Flat and house moves, office relocations, single-item delivery, and pickup-and-drop runs across every London borough. Hourly pricing from £65 with no hidden fees, £2M public liability cover, and a team that knows London streets, lifts and one-way systems.

Get a moving quote →
Call +44 7304 330614

## How much does a man and van cost in London?

A man and van in London costs £65/hr for 1 man + van, £90/hr for 2 men + van and £115/hr for 3 men + a Luton van, with a 3-hour minimum. As a total move, a 1-bed flat usually runs £195–£360, a 2-bed £360–£540 and a studio or single item from £195.

What's included on every Hausio move

No call-out fee. No fuel surcharge inside the M25. No "stairs charge". One transparent hourly rate.

#### Free protective materials

Wardrobe boxes, bubble wrap, TV/glass blankets and mattress covers are provided free. Standard moving boxes are £2.50 each, or bring your own.

#### Stairs & lifts included

Up to 4 floors of stairs is part of the hourly rate — no extra "walk-up charge" that some Greater London man-and-van firms still add.

#### Goods-in-transit insurance

£25,000 cover per move, plus £2M public liability for the building. For high-value tech, fine art or antiques, declare the value at booking.

#### Disassembly & reassembly

Bed frames, IKEA wardrobes, dining tables — we take them apart at pickup and put them back together at the destination, included.

Man and van FAQ

Q: How much does a man with a van cost in London?

1 man + van starts at £65/hr with Hausio (3-hour minimum). 2 men + van £90/hr, 3 men + van £115/hr. A larger Luton van adds £15/hr. Bookings inside the Congestion Zone (EC, WC, W1, SW1, SE1) carry a flat £18 access charge.

Q: How long does a 1-bed flat move take in London?

Usually 3–4 hours door-to-door with 1 man + van; 2–3 hours with 2 men. Stairs (no-lift Victorian buildings), parking distance and heavy furniture are the biggest variables.

Q: Can you do a same-day move?

Same-day single-item delivery and small studio/1-bed moves are usually possible in Zones 1–3 if booked before 11:00. Larger 2-bed and house moves need 24–48 hours' notice.

## Before you book

A few details help us plan your visit and give you a clearer estimate.

### Choose your crew
1 mover + van: £65/hr, £195 minimum. 2 movers + van: £90/hr, £270 minimum. Tell us about bulky items so we can confirm the right crew.

### Plan the route and access
Prepare both postcodes, an item list or photos, floors, lift access and parking details at each address.

### Understand the estimate
Minimum 3 hours. Every hour has the same rate: 4 hours costs £260 with 1 mover or £360 with 2. Selected extras and access charges are additional.

## How much does a handyman cost in London?

A handyman in London costs £65 for the first hour then £50/hour with Hausio, with no call-out fee and nothing to pay until the job is done. A half-day (4 hours) is £215 and a full day (8 hours) £395. Most small jobs — a few shelves, a TV mount, a leaking tap — are finished within the first hour or two.

Handyman FAQ

Q: How much does a handyman charge per hour in London?

Hausio charges £65 first hour, £50 each additional hour, 2-hour minimum booking. Half-day £215, full day £395. The rate covers a fully insured handyman with their own toolkit; specialist materials are billed at cost.

Q: Can a Hausio handyman assemble IKEA furniture?

Yes. Rough guide: Malm bed ~45 min, Pax wardrobe 1.5–2h, Hemnes 4-drawer ~30 min, Kallax 4×4 ~25 min. Bring the assembly fittings; we'll bring everything else.

Q: Can I book a handyman for a list of small jobs?

That's our most popular booking. A half-day at £215 usually covers 8–12 small tasks across a 1-bed flat — shelves, blinds, hooks, tap aerators, door alignment, etc.

## How much do building works cost?
Building work is priced per project after we review photos, measurements, access and the required finish. Larger or structural work may need a site visit, drawings, permissions or specialist input before the quote can be confirmed. You receive the agreed scope and price before work starts.

Building Works FAQ

Q: Do you give an hourly building rate?
Building projects vary too much for one honest hourly headline. We price the agreed project after reviewing the scope, materials, access and finish.

Q: Can Hausio carry out foundation work?
Yes, subject to inspection and the correct specification. Structural foundation work must follow the engineer's design and applicable Building Control requirements before work begins.

Q: Do you supply tiles, wallpaper and glass?
We can price supply or work with customer-supplied finishes. The quote states quantities, allowances and who purchases each item.

Q: Is glazing certification included?
The quote identifies any safety-glass, Building Regulations or competent-person requirements. Work requiring certification is assigned only through an appropriately qualified route.

### Measurements and access

### Finish and timing
Describe the result, preferred materials and any deadline.

Plumbing FAQ

Q: Do you handle emergency plumbing?
We accept urgent enquiries during our normal hours, 08:00–20:00. Availability and the price are confirmed before attendance.

Q: Can you repair boilers or gas appliances?
Gas and boiler work is only undertaken by a Gas Safe registered engineer. We do not present general plumbing staff as qualified for gas work.

Q: Can you quote from a photo?
Often yes for taps, traps, toilet parts and appliance connections. Hidden leaks or pipe rerouting may need an inspection.

Q: Are parts included?
Parts and materials are listed separately in the quote unless the written scope says they are included.

How a London assembly visit works

01

Furniture assembly FAQ

Q: How much for Pax assembly in London?

A standard Pax frame with two doors is £85 flat-rate. Add £15 per extra pair of doors and £20 for glide-rail drawer kits. Typically 1.5–2 hours' work; tipped into place not lifted, so no cracked side panels in low-ceiling flats.

Q: Do you bring tools?

Yes — drill, hex keys, mallet, spirit level, stud finder, tape measure. You only need to hold on to the IKEA fittings bag (cams, dowels, screws) — those are model-specific.

Q: What if parts are missing?

We check the manifest before opening the sealed fittings bag. If anything is genuinely missing, we stop at the latest safe stage, log the IKEA part number, and return for a short follow-up at £45 once you've reordered the spare — no second minimum.

TV mounting FAQ

Q: How much to mount a 55-inch TV?

£75 fixed in London, whether the wall is plasterboard, brick or reinforced concrete. Add £40 for in-wall cable concealment, £20 for surface trunking on solid masonry.

Q: Can you mount above a fireplace?

Yes, but we'll usually try to talk you out of it. Heat above an active fire voids most TV warranties, and the viewing angle is bad for your neck. On a sealed electric or decorative-only chimney breast it's fine — a tilt bracket helps. For active fires, a side-of-chimney pull-out arm is the better solution.

Q: Do you supply brackets?

Either way works. Bring your own, or we bring one at trade cost — £25–£60 for fixed/tilt, £80–£140 for full-motion arms. No markup. If you've already got one, send us the model number so we can confirm the VESA and weight rating.

Why a licence matters

Most £40-a-van Facebook clearance ads aren't licensed. If your garden waste turns up fly-tipped on a verge in Enfield, the fine traces back to you.

#### Upper Tier Waste Carrier Licence

Issued by the Environment Agency. We're on the public register — verifiable before you book, name on the side of the van.

#### Transfer note for every job

You get a Duty of Care waste transfer note by email after the job — proof you handed it to someone licensed. Keep it for 2 years.

#### Tip fees included

The price you see covers labour, fuel, AND the per-tonne tip charge at a registered transfer station. No "extra disposal fee" sprung at the end.

#### Conservation-area aware

If a tree has a Tree Preservation Order (TPO) or sits in a conservation area, we'll flag it before we start — felling without LPA consent is a £20,000 fine.

Garden clearance FAQ

Q: Are you a licensed waste carrier?

Yes — Upper Tier Waste Carrier Licence from the Environment Agency, transfer notes issued for every job. Important: under the Environmental Protection Act 1990, if waste handed to an unlicensed carrier is later fly-tipped, the householder is liable for the fine, not the van.

Q: Can you take garden waste only?

Yes. Pure green waste (cuttings, soil, turf, prunings) goes to a green-waste transfer station with lower tip fees — we pass the saving on. Tell us at booking what's in the load so we can route it correctly.

Q: How much for a 1-bed flat back garden?

A typical small London back garden — shrubs, a collapsed shed, some pots, a broken chair — usually fits a quarter to half-load: £120–£180 including labour, tip and transfer note. Stumps, slabs and hot tubs are quoted as add-ons from a photo.

Why a licensed waste carrier matters

It's the single biggest difference between a £60 Facebook van and an Environment-Agency-registered firm — and the difference shows up if anything goes wrong.

#### Householder liability stays with you

Under the Environmental Protection Act 1990, the householder is responsible for ensuring waste is given to a licensed carrier. Unlicensed van fly-tips it? You get the fine.

#### Transfer note in your inbox

Every Hausio job ends with an emailed waste transfer note showing what was collected, our CBDU number, and the registered transfer station. Keep it 2 years.

#### Landlords & businesses

If you're a landlord or running a business, you're legally required to have transfer notes on file. We format ours for landlord/agency record-keeping by default.

#### Tip fees, never extras

Quoted price includes the per-tonne tip charge at the transfer station. We don't sting you with a "disposal fee" at the end of the job once the van's loaded.

Painter vs handyman — when to call who

A handyman can touch up scuffs and repaint a single wall. For whole rooms, full flats and any period property work, you want a painter.

#### Prep is 70% of the job

Taping, filling, sanding, priming. If a painter shows up and starts rolling on day one, hire someone else — that finish will be flaking by the second winter.

#### Ceiling stain? Find the leak first

A new white ceiling won't hide a slow leak from the flat upstairs. We'll flag it before we paint, and you'll want a plumber to sort the source before we coat over.

#### Conservation areas & listed flats

External facade colours in Westminster, Kensington & Chelsea, Camden CAs need Listed Building Consent or planning sign-off. We won't touch a facade colour-change without it.

#### Materials, honest

Dulux Trade for landlord-spec, Crown for mid-range, Farrow & Ball or Little Greene where the spec calls for it. Receipts come with the invoice. No markup on paint.

Painting & decorating FAQ

Q: Do you supply paint?

Either way. Bring your own colours (Farrow & Ball, Little Greene, whatever) and we work from it; or we buy at trade cost, no markup — Dulux Trade for landlord-spec, Crown for mid-range, F&B where called for. Receipts come with the invoice.

Q: How long for a 1-bed flat?

~3 days with one painter, ~2 days with two. Walls in reasonable condition. Strip wallpaper, woodchip removal or heavy filling adds a day. Prep is 70% of the job — anyone skipping it is selling you a finish that won't last.

Q: Can you paint over wallpaper?

Sometimes. Well-stuck, smooth (non-textured) paper can be primed and painted — fine for a quick pre-let refresh. Bubbled, peeling, woodchip or embossed paper needs to come off (or be skimmed over) first. We tell you straight on viewing.

## Before you book

A few details help us plan your visit and give you a clearer estimate.

### Describe the rooms
Share room dimensions and whether walls, ceilings, doors or woodwork need painting.

### Show the condition
Send photos of cracks, peeling paint or stains so preparation can be included in the estimate.

### Choose the finish
Tell us your colours, whether you have paint, and when the rooms will be available.

## One room or the whole flat — done properly.

Send room photos and the colour spec. We'll quote a fixed price.

About Hausio — Vetted, Insured London Home Services

About Hausio

# One trusted team for everything your London home needs.

Hausio is a London home-services company started by two cleaners who, through moving jobs, built a team of professionals they trusted. Man and van, handyman, cleaning and specialist jobs — furniture assembly, TV mounting, garden clearance, waste removal and painting. One booking, vetted people, one bill.

Get an instant estimate →
Message us on WhatsApp

Our story

## Hausio started with two cleaners and a van.

Before Hausio had a name, it was two of us cleaning London homes and helping people move.

### Two cleaners, one standard

We began as two cleaning specialists working London homes ourselves: end-of-tenancy cleans, deep cleans, weekly visits. We learned what a home actually needs by doing the work with our own hands, and we kept one rule from day one: leave a place the way we would want our own home left.

### Moving days brought the team together

Moving jobs took us into flats and houses across the city, and on those days we kept meeting the same kind of people: handymen, movers and cleaners who turned up on time, did the job properly and cared about the result. Over time that circle became a team of professionals we trusted with our own customers.

### Why we opened our own company

We started Hausio so that people could spend their time living, not cleaning, packing or fixing. One trusted team, one booking, clear prices and £0 to pay until the job is done. That is the company we wanted to hire ourselves, so we built it.

Why people trust us

#### Vetted & DBS-checked

Every person who enters your home is DBS-checked, interviewed in person and reference-verified before their first job — no anonymous gig-workers sent to your door.

#### Fully insured

£2M public liability cover on every job, plus £25,000 goods-in-transit cover on moves. If something goes wrong, you're protected from the moment we arrive.

#### Pay after the job

£0 at booking. You only pay once the work is done and you're happy with it — by card, Apple Pay or Google Pay. No upfront deposit, no cash needed.

How Hausio works

Built to take the friction out of getting something done at home.

### One team, many jobs

Most homes don't need a specialist firm for every little thing. Hausio brings man and van, handyman and cleaning under one roof, so a move, a repair and an end-of-tenancy clean can be one coordinated booking instead of three.

### Clear pricing before you submit

You see the rate, minimum booking time and selected extras before you submit — handyman from £65 for the first hour, man and van from £65/hour and TV mounting from £55. We confirm the final quote after reviewing the job details.

### Local, all over London

We work across all 32 London boroughs, seven days a week from 8am to 8pm. Our teams know the parking zones, the estate lifts and the conservation rules street by street — so access is sorted before we arrive, not argued about on the day.

Company details

## Who you are actually dealing with.

Every claim on this page can be checked against a public register.

Title: Hausio FAQ — Pricing, Booking, Payment & Coverage in London

Hausio FAQ — Pricing, Booking, Payment & Coverage in London

Skip to content

FAQ

# Everything you might want to ask, answered.

Pricing, booking, insurance and how you pay — the honest answers, in plain English. Can't find yours? Message us on WhatsApp and we'll help.

Pricing & fees

Q: How much do home services cost in London?

Cleaning from £30/hr one-off, £27/hr regular and £45/hr deep, with a 5-hour minimum. Man and van starts at £65/hr for one mover and £90/hr for two movers, with a 3-hour minimum. Handyman is £65 for the first hour and £50/hr after, with a 2-hour minimum. Furniture assembly starts at £45/hr, TV mounting at £55, garden clearance at £120, waste removal at £55 and painting at £220/day. Building works, plumbing and garden maintenance are quoted separately after the scope, access and materials are reviewed.

Q: Are there any hidden fees or call-out charges?

There is no call-out fee. Before you submit, the estimator itemises the service rate, minimum booking time and any options you select. Depending on the job, extras can include cleaning products, larger-home supplements, moving mileage or packing, an £18 Central London access charge, and a £15 same-day surcharge. We confirm the final quote after reviewing the details.

Q: Do you charge for a quote?

Never. Quotes are free, and there's £0 to pay at booking — you only pay once the work is done and you're happy with it.

Booking & coverage

Q: How do I book Hausio?

Book online in about 60 seconds — choose your service, enter your postcode and pick a date. Prefer to talk it through? Message us on WhatsApp and we'll arrange it for you.

Q: Can I get a same-day booking in London?

Usually, yes. Book before 10am and we can normally fill a same-day slot in Zones 1–3. A £15 same-day surcharge applies. For guaranteed availability, book at least 24 hours ahead.

Q: Can I reschedule or cancel?

Yes — just let us know ahead of time and we'll move or cancel your slot, no fuss. Because there's £0 to pay at booking, changing plans costs you nothing.

Q: What days and hours are you available?

Seven days a week, 8am to 8pm — weekends included.

Q: Which areas of London do you cover?

All 32 London boroughs, with Zones 1–3 as our core. Wherever you are in Greater London, a vetted team is usually 15–30 minutes away. See our how it works page for the full process.

Trust & insurance

Q: Are your team members vetted and insured?

Yes. Every Hausio team member is DBS-checked, interviewed in person and reference-verified, and we carry £2M public liability insurance plus £25,000 goods-in-transit cover on every job.

Q: Who actually turns up?

A vetted Hausio professional — not an anonymous gig-worker. They arrive on time with the right tools and know the local parking, access and building quirks, so the job just gets done.

Q: What if I'm not happy with the work?

Tell us and we'll put it right. Because you pay only after the work is complete and you're satisfied, you're never out of pocket for a job that isn't right.

Payment

Q: Do I pay a deposit?

No. There's £0 to pay at booking — you settle only once the job is finished and you're satisfied.

Q: How and when do I pay?

You pay after the visit, once the work is done, by card, Apple Pay or Google Pay. No cash required and no upfront deposit.

Services & the practical stuff

Q: What services does Hausio offer?

Man and van, handyman, cleaning, furniture assembly, TV wall mounting, garden clearance, waste removal and painting & decorating — across all of London.

Q: Do you bring your own tools and products?

Yes. Our teams arrive with the right tools and equipment, and cleaning uses eco-friendly products as standard. If a job needs specific materials or a bracket, we supply them at cost — never marked up.

Q: Do you handle office or commercial jobs?

Yes — small office relocations, office furniture clearance, commercial waste removal and similar. Just tell us the details when you book and we'll quote it.

Q: What about parking and the Congestion Charge?

We handle it. Where a controlled parking zone applies, a tradesperson permit is built into the quote; and inside the Central London Congestion Zone (EC, WC, W1, SW1, SE1) a flat £18 access charge applies — shown up front, so there are never surprise charges on the day.

## Still have a question?

Message us on WhatsApp or get an instant estimate — either way, £0 today and you pay after the job.

Title: Building Works in London: Services, Quotes & Project Planning | Hausio

Building Works in London: Services, Quotes & Project Planning | Hausio

Skip to content

Guide · Building Works

# Building works in London: what Hausio does and how project quotes work.

Published 10 September 2026 · 7 min read · By Serhii Perepechaiev, Hausio

Hausio provides building works across Greater London, including tiling, wallpapering, selected groundworks and foundation-related work, exterior repairs, glazing and interior finishing. There is no single honest hourly price for this mix of work. Each job is reviewed and quoted separately so the customer can see the agreed scope before work begins.

This guide explains which jobs fit the service, what information produces an accurate quotation and when drawings, permissions or a specialist are likely to be needed.

## What building work can Hausio arrange?

The service covers practical improvements and repairs inside and outside London homes. Typical enquiries fall into five groups:

Tiling: kitchen splashbacks, bathroom walls and floors, replacement tiles, grout renewal, silicone and finishing.

- Wallpaper and interior finishes: wallpaper removal and hanging, lining paper, feature walls and preparation before decorating.

- Groundworks and foundations: excavation, concrete bases, pads, drainage preparation and foundation-related work completed to an agreed specification.

- Exterior work: brickwork repairs, pointing, rendering, steps, paths, small masonry jobs and surface preparation.

- Glazing: measuring, replacing and fitting glass for windows, doors and internal panels, including safety glass where the specification requires it.

Customers can combine related jobs in one request. For example, a bathroom project may include substrate preparation, tiling, silicone and the fitting of bathroom furniture. The quotation separates the stages so both sides know what is included.

## Why building work is priced by project

Two rooms with the same floor area can require very different amounts of work. Existing surfaces may need repair, tiles may need complex cuts, upper-floor access may require extra protection, and exterior jobs depend on weather and access. A fixed headline rate would hide those differences.

Hausio builds the quote from the labour, preparation, materials, access, waste and required finish. If opening up the area could reveal hidden damage, that risk is identified before the job starts. Any change to the agreed scope is discussed and priced before extra work proceeds.

## What to send for an accurate building quote

A useful first message should include the postcode, clear photographs of the whole area and close-ups, approximate measurements, the result you want and any preferred materials. Add plans or a specification if you already have them. For glazing, include the visible glass dimensions and photographs of the frame; final measurements may still need to be taken on site.

Access matters in London. Mention the floor level, lift, parking restrictions, side or garden access and whether materials must pass through a finished part of the home. This helps the team plan protection, deliveries and waste removal.

## Tiling and wallpaper: preparation decides the finish

Good tiling begins below the tile. The surface must be stable, reasonably level and suitable for the chosen adhesive and finish. Wallpaper also depends on preparation: loose material, uneven joints and moisture problems should be addressed before the final covering goes on. Photographs help with an initial estimate, while the condition of the substrate is confirmed before installation.

## Foundations, exterior work and glazing

Foundation-related work must follow the relevant design and site requirements. Where structural input, Building Control or other approval applies, the necessary information must be in place before construction begins. Hausio can review the practical scope, but an informal site conversation does not replace an engineer's design or a required approval.

Exterior work is quoted with access, weather exposure and compatible materials in mind. Glazing is assessed for the correct glass type, location and fitting method. Work that requires certification or a specialist route is assigned accordingly and identified in the quote.

## How the Hausio process works

- Send the project: share photos, measurements, postcode, timing and plans if available.

- Scope review: Hausio checks access, materials, preparation and whether a survey or specialist input is needed.

- Written quotation: you receive the proposed work, price and stated exclusions before agreeing a start date.

- Delivery and handover: the work follows the agreed sequence and the finished area is reviewed with you.

## Get a quote for building works in London

See the full list of services and the information needed for a quotation on the Hausio building works page. Sending good photos and measurements at the start is the fastest way to receive a useful answer.

Quick answers

## Building Works FAQ

Q: How does Hausio price building work in London?
Building work is quoted by project after Hausio reviews the scope, photos, measurements, access, materials and required finish. Larger or structural jobs may need a site survey before the written quote is confirmed.

Q: What building services does Hausio provide?
Hausio provides tiling, wallpapering and interior finishes, groundworks and foundation-related work, exterior repairs and improvements, and glazing across London.

Q: Can Hausio work from my plans or material list?
Yes. Customers can send plans, measurements, finish references and a material list. The written scope states what Hausio supplies, what the customer supplies and any specialist requirements.

## Planning building work in London?

Send photos, measurements, your postcode and any drawings. Hausio will review the scope and prepare a project-specific quotation.

Request a building quote

Cleaning · Pricing

# How much does end-of-tenancy cleaning cost in London? 2026 price guide.

Published 30 April 2026 · Updated 10 September 2026 · 6 min read · By Serhii Perepechaiev, Hausio

Hausio end-of-tenancy cleaning in London is £32 per hour with a five-hour minimum per cleaner. The final total depends on condition, property size and agreed extras; the estimate is shown before booking.

## Hausio end-of-tenancy cleaning prices in 2026

The current Hausio rate is £32 per hour per cleaner, with a five-hour minimum. That makes the minimum labour booking £160. Longer jobs remain at the same hourly rate:

### Example labour totals

5 billable hours£160

- 6 billable hours£192

- 8 billable hours£256

- 10 billable hours£320
Examples at £32/hour; the property estimate is confirmed before booking.

### Common quoted items

- Oven and fridge interiorsIncluded

- Hausio cleaning products+£15/visit

- Central London access+£18 where applicable

- Same-day booking+£15 where available
Larger homes and extra tasks are itemised in the estimate.

Two cleaners can reduce the elapsed time, but billing is based on total cleaner-hours. For example, two cleaners working for four hours equal eight cleaner-hours.

## What changes the number of hours?

Condition has more impact than floor area alone. Built-up oven grease, bathroom limescale, crowded cupboards, pet hair and fine renovation dust all add time. Clear access, an empty fridge and freezer, and removal of personal belongings help the team work through the checklist without pauses.

Photos taken before booking help Hausio estimate the work. The estimate should show the likely hours, optional products, extra tasks and any Central London access charge.

## What an end-of-tenancy clean covers

#### Kitchen
Oven, hob, extractor, fridge and freezer interiors, accessible cupboards and drawers, worktops, sink, taps, splashbacks and floor.

#### Bathrooms
Bath or shower, screens, accessible grout and silicone, taps, toilet, basin, mirrors, fittings and floor.

#### Living rooms and bedrooms
Accessible surfaces, skirting, doors, switches, sockets, wardrobes, interior window glass and floors or carpets.

#### Hallways and stairs
Dusting, vacuuming or mopping, skirting, doors, handrails and reachable fittings.

Balconies, exterior windows, carpet extraction, upholstery and specialist stain treatment should be agreed separately where needed.

## How long should you allow?

A well-kept one-bedroom flat may fit into five to seven cleaner-hours. A larger property or a home with heavy kitchen and bathroom build-up can require substantially longer. Send current photographs instead of relying only on bedroom count.

## Professional cleaning and tenancy deposits

In England, a landlord or agent cannot require a tenant to pay a separate prohibited fee for a third-party cleaning service. The tenant may still need to return the property to the cleanliness recorded at check-in, allowing for fair wear and tear. The government's Tenant Fees Act guidance explains the permitted-payment framework.

For a deposit deduction, records matter: retain the check-in inventory, dated before-and-after photographs, the cleaner's invoice and the check-out report. The future Private Rented Sector Landlord Ombudsman is part of the Renters' Rights Act programme, but the government's current roadmap expects mandatory landlord membership in 2028. It should not be presented as a live shortcut for cleaning-deposit disputes in 2026.

## Before the cleaners arrive

- Remove belongings and rubbish unless removal is part of the booking.

- Defrost and empty the freezer if it must be cleaned inside.

- Provide access to cupboards, appliances and utility areas.

- Share the agent or inventory checklist before the visit.

- Identify fragile finishes, existing damage and areas requiring specialist products.

## Book an end-of-tenancy clean in London

Use the Hausio London cleaning page or booking calculator for an itemised estimate. The public Hausio pricing page is the current source for rates and minimum booking times.

## Book a London end-of-tenancy clean today

£32/hour, with a 5-hour minimum per cleaner. £0 today, pay after the job. Free 72-hour re-clean. Photo evidence as standard.

Garden Maintenance London: Seasonal Care & Quote Guide | Hausio

Guide · Garden Maintenance

# Garden maintenance in London: a practical seasonal guide for smaller gardens.

Published 10 September 2026 · 6 min read · By Serhii Perepechaiev, Hausio

Hausio provides one-off and regular garden maintenance across Greater London, including lawn mowing, edging, accessible hedge trimming, light pruning, weeding, border care, leaf collection and seasonal tidy-ups. The service is quoted for the garden because size, access, growth and green-waste volume change the time required.

Compact London gardens often need frequent light care more than occasional heavy work. A realistic plan keeps paths usable, plants within their space and maintenance visits predictable.

## What garden maintenance includes

Lawns and edges: mowing, edge trimming and agreed light seasonal care.

- Hedges and shrubs: accessible trimming, shaping, removal of dead growth and light pruning.

- Beds and borders: weeding, hoeing, tidying and basic care around established planting.

- Seasonal tidy-ups: leaf collection, cutting back suitable growth and preparing the garden for the next season.

- Regular visits: a repeat task list adjusted for growth and the time of year.

## One-off tidy-up or regular gardener?

A one-off visit suits a garden that needs to be brought back under control before guests, a tenancy change or a season. Regular maintenance suits customers who want the lawn, edges, hedges and borders kept consistently neat.

Fortnightly visits can make sense during faster spring and summer growth. Monthly care may suit a smaller, slower-growing or low-maintenance garden. The right frequency depends on the planting and the finish you expect, so Hausio confirms it after reviewing recent photos.

## A simple seasonal maintenance plan

### Spring

Spring work usually starts with clearing winter debris, defining lawn edges, weeding beds and assessing shrubs before active growth. The task list should prioritise what needs room, light and access rather than cutting every plant in the same way.

### Summer

Lawns and hedges may need more frequent attention. Visits focus on mowing, edges, controlled trimming, weeds and keeping paths and seating areas usable. Watering arrangements remain the customer's decision unless specifically included.

### Autumn

Leaf collection, suitable cutting back and clearing paths become more important. This is also a good point to separate routine green waste from a larger garden-clearance job.

### Winter

Growth slows, so the focus shifts to access, debris, storm damage visible from the ground and planning the next season. Major tree work and specialist climbing sit outside routine maintenance.

## Garden maintenance versus garden clearance

Maintenance covers repeat care such as mowing, trimming, pruning and weeding. Clearance deals with a large initial volume: accumulated waste, unwanted outdoor items, dismantled materials or a garden that requires substantial cutting back. If both are needed, the quotation can separate the clearance from the ongoing maintenance plan. Hausio also has a dedicated garden clearance service.

## What to send for a garden quote

Send recent wide photographs from several angles, close-ups of hedges or problem areas, the postcode and an approximate garden size. Show the route from the street to the garden, especially if tools and waste must pass through the home. Say whether there is an outdoor power point and how much green waste is already present.

The written quote should state the task list, whether the visit is one-off or regular, and how bagging and removal of green waste will be handled.

## When a tree specialist is needed

Routine garden maintenance can cover accessible shrubs, hedges and light work on small trees from ground level. Large trees, protected trees, difficult branches and any work needing specialist climbing, permissions or advanced equipment require an appropriately qualified tree professional. Send photos so this can be identified before booking.

## Arrange garden maintenance in London

Visit the Hausio garden maintenance page to see the service scope and request a one-off or regular quotation. Recent photos, access details and the result you want are the best starting point.

Quick answers

## Garden Maintenance FAQ

Q: What does Hausio garden maintenance include?
Hausio garden maintenance can include lawn mowing and edging, accessible hedge trimming, light pruning, weeding, border care, leaf collection and seasonal tidy-ups.

Q: Does Hausio offer regular garden visits in London?
Yes. One-off, fortnightly or monthly visits can be quoted after the garden, access, seasonal growth and preferred level of finish have been reviewed.

Q: Is green waste removal included?
Green waste bagging and removal can be included, but the amount and disposal requirement should be shown in the written quote. Large clearance jobs are handled separately from routine maintenance.

## Want a garden that stays manageable?

Send recent photos, your postcode and whether you need a one-off tidy-up or regular visits. Hausio will prepare a garden-specific quote.

Title: Handyman London 2026: Rates, Common Jobs & Hiring Tips — Hausio

Handyman London 2026: Rates, Common Jobs & Hiring Tips — Hausio

Skip to content

Guide · Handyman

# Hiring a handyman in London: the complete 2026 guide.

Published 26 July 2026 · 5 min read · By Nikita Denysiuk, Hausio

Hiring a handyman in London should be the easiest home job you ever book: one visit, a list of small fixes, a fair hourly rate. In practice it is where people get caught out most — the shelf that never sits level, the TV mount that pulls a chunk out of a plasterboard wall, the "quick job" that quietly becomes a lost afternoon. This is a practical guide to what a good London handyman actually does in 2026, what the work really costs, and how to tell a dependable tradesperson from the noise when you search "handyman near me".

## The jobs a London handyman actually gets booked for

Most call-outs are not one big task — they are a punch list of small ones. The regulars we see across the city:

Shelves and picture hanging — the most common request, and the one most often botched. In a Victorian conversion the walls are rarely true, so anything mounted needs proper packing and the right fixings.

- Flat-pack and furniture assembly — IKEA wardrobes, beds and Kallax units, from £45/hour with flat rates on common models.

- TV wall mounting — where the wall itself decides the job (more below).

- Sealing and silicone — baths, sinks and shower trays. London's hard water chews through cheap sealant, so this comes round more often than people expect.

- Skirting, door easing and adjustments — timber doors swell in older flats; a few millimetres planed off stops the sticking.

- Minor plumbing and electrics — tap washers, aerators, waste traps, light fittings, a new socket faceplate. A good handyman also knows the line: anything notifiable under Part P, or any gas work, goes to a registered electrician or a Gas Safe engineer.

TV mounting is the job where London's building stock changes everything. Drill into solid Victorian brick and you want masonry plugs and a decent bracket; drill into a plasterboard stud partition — standard in newer conversions and loft rooms — and you must hit the timber studs or use proper cavity fixings, or the screen ends up on the floor. A handyman who reaches for a stud detector before the drill is telling you something.

## Handyman rates in London in 2026

Honest handyman rates in London are hourly for general work and fixed for defined tasks. Ours:

- £65 for the first hour, then £50 per hour, with a two-hour minimum.

- Half-day (4 hours) £215. Full day (8 hours) £395.

- Furniture assembly is billed at the same handyman rates.

- TV wall mounting is fixed by screen size: up to 43" £55, 44–55" £75, 56–65" £95, 66–85" £150.

Materials — screws, fixings, sealant, a bracket if you need one — are charged at cost, never marked up. Jobs inside the Central London Congestion Zone (EC, WC, W1, SW1, SE1) carry a flat £18 access charge that covers the daily Congestion Charge, and a same-day booking adds £15. Everything is quoted before we start, so there are no surprises on the invoice.

## Day rate versus hourly: which to book

The rule of thumb: book by the hour for one or two defined jobs, and by the day once the list gets long. Two or three fixes — a shelf, a blind, a dripping tap — sit comfortably inside the two-hour minimum. A flat's worth of snags, say eight to twelve small items, is a half-day at £215. A full move-in checklist, or a room being brought back to order, is where the £395 full day earns its keep, working out cheaper per hour than booking piecemeal. Send a short list at booking with a photo per job and the visit can be planned properly rather than discovered on the doorstep.

## What a good handyman should have

Three things separate a professional from a bloke with a drill. First, they are vetted: every Hausio handyman is DBS-checked and interviewed in person before they set foot in a home. Second, they are insured — £2M public liability and £25k goods-in-transit — so if something goes wrong, it is covered. Third, they carry the right tools and know their limits: a good handyman turns down the jobs that legally belong to a certified electrician or a Gas Safe engineer rather than bodging them.

## Red flags worth avoiding

- Cash only, no invoice. No paper trail means no recourse.

- A firm price for a vague list, sight unseen. Either it is padded, or corners get cut when the job runs long.

- No insurance they can name. Ask for the cover; a real firm answers in seconds.

- Full payment demanded upfront. You should never pay before the work is done — with Hausio it is £0 at booking, and you pay by card, Apple Pay or Google Pay only once the job is finished.

- Drilling without checking for cables or pipes. A cheap detector prevents an expensive flood or a dead ring main.

## How coverage works across London boroughs

Hausio covers Greater London, with Zones 1–3 as the core, seven days a week from 8am to 8pm, and you can book online in about sixty seconds. Coverage is genuinely local. The same team knows that a handyman in Wandsworth job around SW18 Earlsfield or SW11 Battersea usually means a controlled parking zone; that a handyman in Camden call in NW1 or NW5 Kentish Town means tight streets and permit parking; and that a handyman in Islington visit near N1 Angel or N7 Holloway sits inside the same web of CPZs. Parking and access are sorted before the visit, not argued about on arrival. For the full service, fixings and booking, see our London handyman page.

## Book a London handyman today

£65 for the first hour, then £50/hr, two-hour minimum. £0 at booking — pay after the job by card, Apple Pay or Google Pay. Every handyman is DBS-checked and fully insured, seven days a week, 8am–8pm.

Title: IKEA Flat-Pack Furniture Assembly in London: 2026 Guide — Hausio

IKEA Flat-Pack Furniture Assembly in London: 2026 Guide — Hausio

Skip to content

Guide · Furniture Assembly

# IKEA and flat-pack furniture assembly in London: the 2026 guide.

Published 26 July 2026 · 5 min read · By Nikita Denysiuk, Hausio

A flat-pack box looks simple on the shop floor and considerably less so at 9pm on the living-room carpet, surrounded by cam locks, dowels and a wordless manual. IKEA flat-pack assembly in London carries an extra layer of difficulty most buying guides skip: the flat itself. This is a practical guide to furniture assembly in London in 2026 — what a good service actually builds, how long each piece really takes, and why a Victorian conversion in N16 turns the same PAX wardrobe into twice the job it would be in a Home Counties new-build.

## What an IKEA assembly service actually builds

Most bookings fall into a handful of categories. An IKEA assembly service spends its weeks on bedroom storage above everything else — PAX wardrobes (frames, hinged and sliding doors, KOMPLEMENT internals), MALM and HEMNES chests, and bed frames from MALM up to the taller BRIMNES with underbed drawers.

Beyond the bedroom, the regular list runs to:

Bunk beds and high sleepers — MYDAL, STUVA and non-IKEA equivalents, the fiddliest common build

- Desks and home-office kit, from a plain LAGKAPTEN top to motorised sit-stand frames

- KALLAX and BILLY shelving runs, often wall-anchored across an alcove

- Kitchen units — IKEA METOD carcasses, drawers and door alignment (cabinetry, not plumbing)

- Garden and balcony furniture — the summer rush, usually softwood sets and rattan-effect sofas

The same crew handles Wayfair, Made, Habitat and Argos flat-pack too. Non-IKEA boxes vary far more in quality, which affects both time and price. The full breakdown lives on our furniture assembly London page.

## How long each piece really takes

Manufacturer "assembly times" assume a clear floor, every part present and someone who has built the model before. Real timings for one experienced assembler tend to look like this:

- BILLY bookcase — 20 to 30 minutes

- KALLAX 4x4 — 30 to 45 minutes

- MALM bed or chest — 45 to 90 minutes

- HEMNES dresser — around an hour

- PAX wardrobe, single frame with doors — 1.5 to 2.5 hours; sliding doors add time for alignment

- Bunk bed or high sleeper — 2 to 3 hours

- Sit-stand desk — 45 to 60 minutes

- A run of METOD kitchen units — most of a day

Two things blow those figures out: missing or damaged parts (check the manifest before opening the sealed fittings bag), and access — the subject of the next section.

## Why London flats make flat-pack fiddly

Flat-pack furniture assembly in London is rarely about the box and usually about the building. Three things separate a smooth build from a lost afternoon.

Walls. IKEA supplies an anti-tip restraint with every tall wardrobe and chest, and fixing it correctly is not optional — it is the difference between safe and dangerous furniture. What the wall is made of decides how. Victorian and Edwardian conversions across Hackney, Camden and Tooting are usually solid brick or lath-and-plaster: brick takes a masonry bit and a proper plug; lath-and-plaster needs care to find a joist. Post-2000 new-builds in Nine Elms, Stratford (E20) and Canary Wharf are typically plasterboard on metal studs, or dot-and-dab board over blockwork with a void behind — the wrong fixing there pulls straight out. A PAX anchored into a stud, a spring toggle or the brick behind the void is secure; a screw in bare plasterboard is not.

Getting the box in. Narrow Victorian stairwells, tight half-landings and lift-free walk-ups in N1, SW11 and NW6 mean a 2.4m PAX frame sometimes cannot be turned at the top of the stairs — so it is built flat and walked upright into place, which needs floor space and a second pair of hands. Mansion blocks and new-builds may have a lift, but check whether it is a small passenger lift or a goods lift that has to be booked ahead.

The van and the kerb. If we collect the flat-pack for you, ULEZ, the Congestion Charge and controlled parking zones all apply. A suspended bay or a permit-only street in Islington or Kensington needs planning — there is no loading on a red route.

## Assembled by a pro, or do it yourself?

Self-assembly is genuinely fine for a BILLY or a KALLAX on a free Saturday. The calculation changes with weight, height and anything that anchors to a wall. A PAX is heavy, unforgiving of a single misread diagram, and easy to rack out of square so the doors never sit flush. Bunk beds carry a child's safety on the fixings. Kitchen units have to be dead level or every door looks wrong. If a piece is tall, load-bearing or slept in, the case for a pro is strongest — and you keep the walls undamaged and the packaging cleared.

## What to check before you book

Five things make an assembly visit go cleanly:

- Have the model names or the IKEA receipt to hand — it tells the assembler exactly what is coming

- Confirm the boxes have arrived and are in the room, not still with the courier

- Keep the fittings bags sealed and together — cams and dowels are model-specific

- Flag your wall type and any lift or stairwell issue when booking, so the right fixings come in the van

- Clear roughly two square metres of floor per large item

## What Hausio charges, and how booking works

Hausio prices furniture assembly from £45 an hour with a one-hour minimum, plus flat rates on the most-booked IKEA models — a PAX wardrobe from £85, a MALM bed £45, a HEMNES dresser £35, KALLAX £25 and a BILLY £20. Anything non-IKEA, or a bigger multi-item build, is charged at the same £45 an hour. For the full flat-rate list see our furniture assembly London page.

Every assembler is DBS-checked, interviewed in person and fully insured (£2M public liability, £25k goods-in-transit), and arrives with drill, hex keys, mallet, level and stud finder. Jobs inside the Central London Congestion Zone (EC, WC, W1, SW1 and SE1 postcodes) carry a flat £18 access charge; same-day slots add £15. There is £0 to pay at booking — you settle after the job by card, Apple Pay or Google Pay. Booking online takes about a minute, seven days a week, 8am to 8pm.

## Flat-pack sorted in one visit.

Tell us what's in the box — a PAX wall, a MALM bed, a METOD kitchen run or the lot — and a DBS-checked, fully insured assembler brings the tools, the right wall fixings and the patience. From £45 an hour, one-hour minimum, with flat rates on common IKEA models. £0 at booking, pay after the job by card, Apple Pay or Google Pay.

Title: London Congestion Charge & ULEZ 2026: Home-Service Access Guide — Hausio

London Congestion Charge & ULEZ 2026: Home-Service Access Guide — Hausio

Skip to content

News · Pricing

# London Congestion Charge and ULEZ 2026: a home-service access guide.

Published 30 April 2026 · Updated 10 September 2026 · 4 min read · By Nikita Denysiuk, Hausio

London road charges can affect a home-service visit when a vehicle enters the relevant zone during charging hours. Hausio shows its applicable £18 Central London access charge separately so it is visible before booking.

## Congestion Charge in 2026

Transport for London lists the Congestion Charge as £18 when paid in advance or on the day. Charging hours are 07:00–18:00 Monday to Friday and 12:00–18:00 on Saturdays, Sundays and bank holidays. The charge does not operate during the published Christmas-to-New-Year suspension.

The zone is a defined central-London area, so a postcode alone should not be used as a guarantee that an address is inside or outside it. TfL's official Congestion Charge checker and guidance is the correct source for a specific address.

## ULEZ is a separate scheme

ULEZ operates across all London boroughs, 24 hours a day except Christmas Day. It applies only when a vehicle does not meet the required emissions standard. A compliant vehicle does not pay the daily ULEZ charge.

That distinction matters: the £18 Hausio access charge for applicable central-London work should not be described as a ULEZ charge for a compliant van. It reflects the Congestion Charge and the access planning associated with a central job.

## How the charge appears in a Hausio estimate

The access charge is displayed as its own line where applicable.

- It is not presented as a discount on later moving hours.

- Parking, permits or unusual loading restrictions are assessed separately when the address requires them.

- The service rate and booking minimum remain visible alongside any access charge.

## What to send before a London visit

Provide the complete postcode and building or estate name, the preferred arrival time, parking instructions and any loading-bay or concierge restrictions. For a move, say whether the van can stop near the entrance and whether lifts must be reserved.

See the current Hausio pricing page for service rates and common charges. Borough information for Westminster and Camden can help with local planning, but TfL remains the source for the actual charging boundary.

## Get a transparent London quote in 60 seconds

Cleaning from £27/hr, man and van from £65/hr, handyman from £65 first hour (2-hour minimum). Congestion Zone surcharge always itemised — never hidden.

Title: Plumber London: Repairs, Installations & Quote Guide | Hausio

Plumber London: Repairs, Installations & Quote Guide | Hausio

Skip to content

Guide · Plumbing

# Plumber in London: common repairs, installations and how to get a clear quote.

Published 10 September 2026 · 6 min read · By Nikita Denysiuk, Hausio

Hausio provides plumbing repairs and installations across Greater London for common water, waste and bathroom jobs. This includes leaking taps, sink wastes, toilets, appliance connections, radiator changes and bathroom fittings. The price is confirmed for the specific job after the fault, access and likely parts have been reviewed.

The quickest route to a useful plumbing quote is a clear description supported by photos or a short video. This guide explains what to send, which jobs can often be priced remotely and when an inspection is the sensible next step.

## Common plumbing jobs in London homes

Leaks and drips: visible leaks from taps, exposed pipework, traps, wastes and accessible joints.

- Taps and sinks: tap replacement, cartridges, basin and sink wastes, traps and resealing around fittings.

- Toilets: flush mechanisms, fill valves, seats, seals and selected toilet replacements.

- Appliance connections: washing machines and dishwashers where suitable water, waste and electrical connections already exist.

- Radiators: valve changes, replacement radiators and related water-side work after the system and access are assessed.

- Bathroom finishing: fitting selected sanitary items, shower accessories, waste connections and silicone finishing.

## What to do when you find a leak

If water is escaping quickly, turn off the relevant isolation valve or the property's main stopcock if it is safe and accessible. Move belongings away from the water and avoid electrical fittings or sockets in the affected area. Then send Hausio a photograph or video showing both the leak and the wider installation.

A stain on a ceiling or wall does not always show where the water began. The source can be above or some distance away, so hidden leaks may need investigation before repair work can be quoted accurately.

## Can a plumber quote from a photo?

Visible, defined jobs can often be priced from good photographs. A clear image of the complete tap, trap, toilet cistern or appliance connection helps identify the likely part and the space available to work. Include the make or model where it is visible.

An inspection is more likely when pipework is concealed, the source of a leak is uncertain, access is restricted, several fittings are affected or the proposed installation requires pipe rerouting. The purpose of the visit is to define the repair rather than guess at it.

## How Hausio prepares a plumbing quote

The quote considers labour, likely parts, access and the possibility of further investigation. Materials are listed separately unless the written scope says they are included. If the opened fitting reveals a different fault, the plumber explains the finding and agrees any change before additional work continues.

For the first enquiry, send your postcode, the type of fitting, when the problem started, whether water can be isolated and photos from both close and wider angles. Mention any parking or building-access restrictions.

## Plumbing, boilers and gas work

Water plumbing and gas work are different scopes. Work on gas appliances, gas pipework and boilers must be undertaken by a suitably qualified Gas Safe registered engineer. Hausio does not describe a general plumber as qualified for gas work. If the enquiry involves a boiler or gas appliance, say so immediately so the correct route can be considered.

## Repairs versus planned installations

A repair starts with the fault: what leaks, blocks, fails to fill or no longer operates. A planned installation starts with compatibility: dimensions, connections, water pressure, drainage, wall construction and the item being fitted. Product links and specification sheets help prevent a new tap, sink or radiator arriving without the correct connections or space.

## Book a plumber in London

Visit the Hausio plumbing service page for the full scope, quotation steps and contact options. A short video plus your postcode will usually answer more than a long message without photographs.

Quick answers

## Plumbing FAQ

Q: What plumbing jobs does Hausio handle in London?
Hausio handles common water and waste plumbing jobs such as leaks, taps, sinks, toilets, traps, appliance connections, radiator changes and bathroom fittings.

Q: Can Hausio quote plumbing from photographs?
Often yes for visible taps, traps, toilet parts and appliance connections. Hidden leaks, pipe rerouting or unclear access may require an inspection before the price is confirmed.

Q: Does Hausio carry out gas or boiler work?
Gas appliances and boiler work must be carried out by a Gas Safe registered engineer. General plumbing staff are not presented as qualified for gas work.

## Need a plumber in London?

Send a photo or short video, your postcode and a description of the fault or installation. Hausio will confirm the next step and job-specific quote.

Title: End-of-Tenancy Cleaning, Deposits & Renters' Rights in 2026 — Hausio

End-of-Tenancy Cleaning, Deposits & Renters' Rights in 2026 — Hausio

# Renters' Rights Act 2025: three things that changed for end-of-tenancy cleaning in London.

Published 30 April 2026 · Updated 10 September 2026 · 5 min read · By Nikita Denysiuk, Hausio

End-of-tenancy cleaning disputes are decided by evidence of condition, responsibility and reasonable cost. The Renters' Rights Act 2025 changed important parts of renting in England, but it did not create a special cleaning-dispute limit or replace the deposit-protection process in 2026.

## Can a landlord require professional cleaning?

A landlord or letting agent cannot require a tenant to pay a separate mandatory fee for a third-party cleaning service. The Tenant Fees Act guidance lists the payments that can be required in England; a compulsory cleaning-service fee is not on that list.

The tenant can still be responsible for returning the property to the level of cleanliness recorded at check-in, allowing for fair wear and tear. The practical question is the condition of the property, not whether the tenant used a particular cleaning company.

## What evidence matters in a deposit dispute?

A tenancy deposit remains the tenant's money unless the landlord establishes a justified deduction. For cleaning, the strongest records are the signed check-in inventory, dated check-out photographs, correspondence about specific areas and a reasonable invoice or estimate for putting the property back to its recorded starting condition.

Before cleaning: photograph every room, appliance interior and existing mark.

- After cleaning: repeat the same angles and retain the originals with dates.

- At handover: keep the cleaning invoice, key-return record and any inventory-clerk report.

- If a deduction is proposed: ask which check-in and check-out evidence supports it and how the amount was calculated.

## What did the Renters' Rights Act change?

The Act introduced a wider programme of tenancy reform, including a future Private Rented Sector Database and Landlord Ombudsman. According to the government's implementation roadmap, the database rollout begins from late 2026 and mandatory landlord membership of the Ombudsman is expected in 2028 after the service has been established.

That means the future Ombudsman should not be described as the current route for ordinary cleaning-deposit disputes in September 2026. Where a protected deposit is disputed, tenants and landlords should follow the process of the government-approved deposit scheme holding or insuring that deposit.

## A practical check-out plan

- Read the check-in inventory and make a room-by-room task list.

- Ask the agent whether they have a check-out checklist, without accepting an obligation to buy a named cleaning service.

- Book enough cleaning time for the actual condition of the property.

- Keep dated photographs and an itemised invoice.

- Respond to any proposed deduction with the relevant records rather than general statements.

This article provides general information for England and is not legal advice. For a specific dispute, check your deposit scheme's guidance or seek independent housing advice.

Spring Deep Clean Checklist for London Flats 2026 — Hausio

How-to · Cleaning

# Spring deep clean checklist for London flats — 2026 edition.

Published 30 April 2026 · 3 min read · By Serhii Perepechaiev, Hausio

Spring is when London's hard water build-up, winter dust and radiator-baked grime show up most clearly. Here's a room-by-room deep clean checklist that takes a 2-bed flat from "looks ok" to "actually clean" — typically 5–7 hours done well.

## Kitchen — 2 hours

Empty fridge and freezer, defrost if needed, wipe shelves and seals

- Inside oven, including racks (soak in hot water + bicarbonate)

- Extractor hood and filter — degreaser, then rinse

- Inside cupboards and drawers — empty, vacuum crumbs, wipe

- Tile grout and splashback descale

- Sink, tap, plughole limescale

## Bathroom — 1.5 hours per bathroom

- Descale taps, shower head, glass screen (white vinegar or commercial descaler)

- Re-grout if any tile lines have darkened (wash first, then assess)

- Replace silicone bead around bath/shower if mouldy — DIY-able with a £6 silicone gun

- Toilet hinges, base and behind

- Extractor fan grille

## Living and bedrooms — 1.5 hours

- Move sofas and beds, vacuum underneath and along skirting

- Behind radiators — radiator brush + vacuum on low

- Light fittings, ceiling lamps (turn power off, dust glass, replace bulbs while you're up there)

- Window interiors, frames and sills (microfibre + dilute white vinegar = no streaks)

- Wash curtains or steam them in place

- Skirting boards — damp microfibre top to bottom

## What's worth outsourcing

If you're short on time, the high-ROI tasks to outsource in London are: oven and fridge interior (2 hours of unpleasant work, professionals do it in 45 minutes), limescale (London water is hard — pros bring stronger products), after-radiator dust (specialist tools for cast-iron Victorian radiators in NW1, N16 and SW18 properties).

## How long the whole thing takes

- Studio: 4 hours self / 3 hours professional

- 1-bed flat: 5–6 hours self / 4 hours professional

- 2-bed flat: 7–8 hours self / 5–6 hours professional

- 3-bed house: 10–12 hours self / 7–8 hours professional

Hausio's London deep clean covers everything in this checklist for £45/hour, with a 5-hour minimum and optional eco-friendly products (+£15 per visit). For full pricing and what an agent-spec clean covers, see our 2026 cleaning cost guide.

# TV wall mounting in London: what it costs in 2026, and what's behind your wall

Published 26 July 2026 · 6 min read · By Serhii Perepechaiev, Hausio

A clean TV wall mount looks like a five-minute job. In a London flat it rarely is. The screen is the easy part — the wall behind it decides everything, and London hands you every wall type going: hollow plasterboard on metal studs in a Canary Wharf tower, 150-year-old solid brick in a Victorian terrace, and reinforced concrete you can't get into without an SDS drill. This is a practical guide to TV wall mounting in London in 2026 — what it costs by screen size, which bracket to choose, and how the right fixing keeps a 65-inch screen on the wall for good.

## TV mounting cost in London by screen size

Hausio prices TV installation in London as a fixed job rather than by the hour, so the figure you're quoted is the figure you pay. Price is set by screen size, and it stays the same whether we're drilling into plasterboard, brick or concrete:

Up to 43" — £55

- 44–55" — £75

- 56–65" — £95

- 66–85" — £150

Two charges sit on top of that only where they apply: a flat £18 access charge inside the Central London Congestion Zone (EC, WC, W1, SW1 and SE1 postcodes), and a £15 same-day surcharge if you need a fitter out before 8pm today. Brackets are supplied at cost with no markup, or you can supply your own. Anything non-standard, such as a partition wall that needs a timber batten fitted first, is quoted at standard London handyman rates before any drilling starts, never sprung on you at the end.

## Fixed, tilt or full-motion: choosing the bracket

The bracket matters more than most people expect, both for how the TV sits and for what the wall can safely carry. Three types cover almost every London living room:

- Fixed (flat) mount — holds the screen 2–3cm off the wall for the tidiest, most flush look. Right when the viewing height is already correct and you don't need to reach the ports behind. The cheapest and strongest option.

- Tilt mount — angles the screen down 10–15°. Worth it whenever the TV goes higher than eye level, in a bedroom or above a media unit, and it kills the reflection from a window opposite.

- Full-motion arm — extends and swivels, so you can watch from a galley kitchen, a corner sofa or the dining table. It is heavier and levers hard on the wall, which is exactly why the fixing underneath it is non-negotiable: a full-motion arm anchored into plasterboard alone will pull out. On a stud wall it has to reach solid timber or steel.

## The London problem: what's actually behind your wall

This is where a proper TV installation in London is won or lost. Four wall types come up again and again, each needing a different anchor:

- New-build plasterboard on metal studs — the standard in Canary Wharf (E14), Stratford (E20), Nine Elms and Wembley Park. For a TV installation in Canary Wharf or any Stratford new-build, the partition is a plasterboard skin over hollow metal C-studs. A 55-inch screen must fix into the steel stud with the correct spring-toggle anchors, or onto a timber batten spanning two studs — plasterboard plugs on their own will not hold it.

- Solid London stock brick — Victorian terraces and conversions across Islington, Hackney and Clapham. The chimney breast is the classic spot: solid brick, drilled with a hammer drill and sleeve anchors, keeping the fixings in the brick and out of the soft lime-mortar joints.

- Reinforced concrete — shear walls in the Vauxhall and Battersea towers, and party walls in older mansion blocks. These need an SDS drill, M8 wedge anchors and dust extraction so the drilling doesn't ruin the carpet.

- Period and listed flats — West End mansion blocks around Oxford Street, Marylebone and Fitzrovia, where the lease often bans chasing into walls. Here the answer is a reversible, surface-mounted solution that comes off cleanly at the end of the tenancy.

## Hiding the cables: trunking or in-wall

A mounted TV with cables dangling below it undoes the whole job. There are two honest ways to deal with them, and the right one depends — again — on the wall:

- In-wall concealment — for plasterboard or any hollow cavity. Power and HDMI drop down inside the void through a low-voltage capsule kit to a socket behind your media unit, so nothing shows at all. Mains can't simply be run loose inside a wall, so we use a bridged-socket kit that stays compliant.

- Surface trunking — for solid brick, concrete or any rental where chasing isn't allowed. Slim paintable trunking, colour-matched to the wall, that hides the run and lifts off without damage when you leave.

## What's included, soundbars, and how long it takes

Every Hausio TV wall mounting visit includes the level-set, lifting the screen onto the bracket, a power-on test, an angle check from where you actually sit, and a quick walk-through of the tilt range so you can adjust it later. The cable drop behind the unit is standard, not an extra. If you want a soundbar mounted and aligned beneath the screen — a Sonos Arc or Beam, say — we can mount and align it in the same visit.

Timing is straightforward. A single-screen mount takes 45–90 minutes. Add cable concealment and it's closer to two hours. A full home-cinema set-up — TV, soundbar, Sky or Virgin box relocated, everything hidden — can run to half a day. Every fitter is DBS-checked, interviewed in person and fully insured (£2M public liability), and you pay £0 at booking: settle by card, Apple Pay or Google Pay only once the screen is up and tested. If you've been searching for TV wall mounting near you anywhere in Greater London, you can book online in about 60 seconds, seven days a week, 8am to 8pm.

## Book London TV wall mounting

Fixed price by screen size, from £55, and £0 at booking. Send us the TV model and a photo of the wall — we'll confirm the bracket and the right fixing before we arrive, then you pay by card, Apple Pay or Google Pay once it's up and tested.
